question: In medieval English towns, who relied most on ready-cooked food from cookshops, and why?
answer: The poor, not the rich. A family in one rented room often had no oven, little fuel and nowhere to store food, so a hot pie cost less than cooking. The rich kept kitchens and cooks. By the 1170s London already had a public cookshop on the riverbank, open day and night.
move: Ask who lacks a kitchen before calling ready-made food a luxury.
source: Carlin, Food and Eating in Medieval Europe
reference: Carlin, Fast Food and Urban Living Standards in Medieval England, in Carlin & Rosenthal (eds), Food and Eating in Medieval Europe, Hambledon Press, 1998
